body.claim: `directly_courted` means the symbol is an undefined dynamic symbol of a staged candidate probe that ran and produced a transcript. It does NOT mean every arm of the symbol was driven: a name that is only address-taken, or stored in a dispatch table, is imported exactly as a direct call is. `indirectly_courted` is an explicit, checked edge -- the named entry is itself directly courted by a probe of the named court. `non_observable` is a symbol whose effect no probe can isolate, with the reason and the court that observes its downstream effect. A symbol in none of the three fails this generator by name -- for every stratum that has begun, in-progress or complete, so an export cannot be landed without an edge.
body.definition: a stratum that has begun is one with an obligation ledger on disk; `complete` records whether it has sealed. Every export a begun stratum implements is partitioned below, whether the stratum is in-progress or complete

indirectly_courted.authority: crypto/modes/gcm128.c:1619 -- CRYPTO_gcm128_new allocates the context and calls CRYPTO_gcm128_init on it, which is the only way a caller obtains a GCM context. The probe drives GCM entirely through CRYPTO_gcm128_new, so the initialiser is exercised on every GCM observation.
crypto/modes/ocb128.c:138 -- CRYPTO_ocb128_new calls CRYPTO_ocb128_init and frees the context when it refuses, so the initialiser runs before any OCB observation.
crypto/camellia/cmll_ecb.c:25 -- the decrypt arm of the same facade.

crypto/camellia/cmll_ecb.c:23 -- Camellia_ecb_encrypt's encrypt arm is Camellia_encrypt, and the probe drives Camellia ECB (and every Camellia mode, through the generic engine's block function) directly.

crypto/idea/i_ecb.c:35 -- IDEA_ecb_encrypt calls IDEA_encrypt on the two 32-bit halves it loads from the block; IDEA_decrypt is directly courted because the probe also calls it by name, and this is its sibling only for IDEA_encrypt.
crypto/seed/seed_ecb.c:24 -- the decrypt arm of the same facade.
crypto/whrlpool/wp_dgst.c:82 and :87 -- WHIRLPOOL_Update hands the byte count to WHIRLPOOL_BitUpdate, which is the construction's only update path, so the probe's 1000-byte message drives it.
